issues.issue: The clause promises the Guarantor 'has not used and shall not use any part of the Facility', but the Facility is drawn by the Borrower, not by the Guarantor, under the Credit Agreement. The undertaking may have no subject matter as written.

The waiver says 'to the extent that there may be attributed to the Borrower such an immunity' in a representation otherwise entirely about the Guarantor, which looks like the wrong party name. Whose immunity is waived is left doubtful by that substitution.

'No Default in respect of the Guarantor' uses a term defined in the Credit Agreement by reference to the Borrower's obligations, and this Agreement contains no default provision of its own. What counts as a Default of the Guarantor must be pieced together from other documents.

'terms and conditions that are substantially more favorable to the beneficiary thereof than as are provided by the Guarantor in this Agreement' gives no metric for comparing guarantees of different structure. 'Substantially more favorable' is the operative and unmeasured standard.

A continuing notice covenant is placed inside Article III, whose lead-in states only that the Guarantor 'represents and warrants ... on the date hereof, on the Effective Date and on each other date on which representations and warranties are made'. Whether (m) is a covenant at all, and what remedy attaches, depends on reconciling the two.

The proviso — 'the aforesaid restriction shall not apply to an arms length sale or disposal of its assets or properties' — appears to swallow the prohibition entirely, since almost any disposal can be characterised as arm's length, and 'arms length' is undefined. The covenant may be left with no operative content.

Read with Section 2.01 and the Article III(e) solvency representation, an unlimited arm's-length disposal carve-out would let the Guarantor strip the assets that stand behind the guarantee. That is difficult to reconcile with the Agreement's evident purpose.

This subsection speaks of 'either Guarantor', 'either Guarantee Agreement' and 'the Parent', none of which exists in this instrument — the preamble names a single Guarantor, EGL, and defines no Parent. The provision cannot be applied without importing another document.

The carve-out 'except by a written instrument pursuant to Section 4.12' points to Section 4.12, which is the Notices provision and says nothing about waivers or amendments; there is no waiver-instrument section in the Agreement. The cross-reference cannot be given effect as written.

'any and all stamp, excise, sales or other taxes' places a general catch-all after three specific transactional taxes, and Section 1.02(e) purports to disapply ejusdem generis; whether income or withholding taxes fall within 'other taxes' is open. The reach of the catch-all is the issue.

Section 4.03 bars assignment without 'the prior written consent of the Facility Agent', while Section 4.15 bars it without 'the prior written consent of the Facility Agent and the Lenders'. The two successors-and-assigns provisions state different consent requirements for the same act.

Section 4.08 says the agreement of the parties is 'This Agreement and the other Loan Documents', while Section 4.14 says 'This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement ... and supersedes all prior ... agreements'. The two integration clauses define the integrated whole differently.

The consent is that proceedings 'may be instituted in or (other than by the Guarantor) removed to' the New York courts, permissive language coupled with an asymmetric parenthetical; whether the New York forum is exclusive as against the Guarantor is not stated. The clause is one-sided enough that any genuine ambiguity would be read against the drafting lenders.

The replacement process agent must have 'offices in [New York]' — a bracketed placeholder left unresolved in the execution version — and the paragraph repeatedly reads 'Each of the Guarantor' and 'the Guarantor agree'. The bracket leaves the required location of a substitute agent uncertain.

The inducement sentence refers to extensions of credit 'TO THE COMPANY', a term used nowhere else in the Agreement, which defines the credit party as the Borrower. The mismatch is small but it is in the operative recital of consideration for the waiver.

Notices go to 'the address of the Guarantor set forth below its signature below', but one execution page leaves the address block blank and the other gives a Mauritius address for a company the preamble describes as Cayman-incorporated. Where valid notice must be sent is not fixed by the instrument.

'Each Lender and the Facility Agent, when appointed hereunder, (for itself and not on behalf of any Lender)' is internally garbled — the parenthetical contradicts the plural subject it follows. The break is mechanical and unlikely to alter any obligation.

Section 4.14 declares this Agreement alone the entire agreement, whereas Section 4.08 Integration states that this Agreement 'and the other Loan Documents' represent the parties' agreement and Section 1.01 imports definitions from the Credit Agreement. Whether the other Loan Documents are superseded is a real question.
'the Guarantor shall not the right to assign or transfer' omits a verb, leaving the prohibition to be reconstructed. As written the sentence does not state a restriction.

This requires consent of 'the Facility Agent and the Lenders' for assignment, while Section 4.03 requires only 'the prior written consent of the Facility Agent'; the two duplicate binding-and-benefit provisions impose different conditions. The third-party sentence also excludes non-parties other than the Lenders, sitting awkwardly with the Borrower's role under Section 2.01(a)(ii).
